object_context: Fresh analytic child opened after RH-ANA-002. The active obstruction is no longer positivity of a finite Li prefix or a manifestly positive Suzuki norm. It is the first zeta-specific prime/archimedean cancellation coordinate that must be controlled uniformly in the Li index n. The immediate pre-candidate question is whether exact arithmetic/explicit-formula decompositions localize the root-sensitive part strongly enough to distinguish what unconditional archimedean asymptotics already control from what finite-place or zero-radial information remains.
structural_coordinates: Li's criterion requires lambda_n >= 0 for every positive integer n; finite-index agreement is non-authoritative without a uniform theorem.
Bombieri-Lagarias give exact arithmetic/Guinand-Weil formulas for lambda_n; the formula contains regularized prime/Laurent data and archimedean terms with n-dependent binomial cancellation.

Lagarias' automorphic-L formulation decomposes generalized Li coefficients into an archimedean contribution, a finite-place contribution, and a pole/trivial term; the archimedean contribution has an unconditional n log n plus n asymptotic.
Lagarias relates the finite-place term to an incomplete Li coefficient cut at height comparable to sqrt(n), up to an error of order sqrt(n) log n in the registered theorem.

On RH, each zero contribution has the unit-modulus radial property needed for zero-counting to yield the corresponding incomplete-Li bound; off the line, the Li radial factor can have modulus different from one.

A single off-region zero can influence a finite interval of Li-type coefficients even when aggregate zero-count estimates remain valid; Palojarvi's tau-Li criteria make this rare-defect sensitivity explicit.
Zero-counting and zero-density statements constrain populations of zeros but do not by themselves impose the per-zero radial envelope |rho/(rho-1)|=1 or its equivalent critical-line condition.
The root-sensitive finite-place coordinate may therefore be a weighted horizontal-displacement/radial-control problem rather than a pure zero-counting problem.
Prime truncations inherit two separate hazards: conditional/regularized summation and n-dependent cancellation; finite computational positivity cannot replace a uniform remainder theorem.

The Lagarias-Voros growth dichotomy remains a contrastive global route, but any unconditional growth estimate strong enough to exclude exponential/off-line contributions must be audited for equivalence strength.
equivalent_formulations: RH: every nontrivial zeta zero rho satisfies Re(rho)=1/2.
Li: lambda_n >= 0 for every positive integer n.
Finite-place cut: obtain an unconditional all-n bound on the finite-place/incomplete-Li term strong enough that the known archimedean main term cannot be overturned.
Radial envelope: control the contribution of zeros with |rho/(rho-1)| different from one without assuming that this modulus equals one for every zero.
Prime-side remainder: prove an exact regularized prime/archimedean decomposition with a uniform-in-n signed or absolute remainder estimate that is strictly weaker than RH.
solved_analogues: Stable-mode counting in linear systems: a low density of unstable eigenmodes does not prevent one mode with spectral radius greater than one from dominating long-time powers; counting and radial control are different coordinates.
Parseval/exact-energy identities: a dominant positive main term yields a target sign only after the signed remainder is bounded at the same uniformity level as the target family.
near_solved_analogues: Lagarias' generalized Li coefficient decomposition and incomplete-Li estimates localize finite-place versus archimedean contributions but the strongest small error bound uses RH-sensitive zero geometry.

Palojarvi's explicit tau-Li zero-free-region criteria quantify how finite Li-type signs detect zeros outside a radial region, illustrating that rare off-region zeros cannot be replaced by aggregate zero counts.
Voros' Li asymptotic dichotomy distinguishes RH-compatible tempered growth from off-line non-tempered oscillation but does not supply the needed unconditional zeta bound.

method_transfers.method: separate the exact Li coefficient into archimedean and finite-place pieces, use unconditional asymptotics only where source-proved, and treat the finite-place/incomplete-Li term as the first residual rather than optimizing the total formula blindly
shared_structure: one component has a controlled deterministic main asymptotic while another contains root-sensitive zero/prime cancellation
required_assumptions: preserve Lagarias' summation and normalization conventions
distinguish unconditional estimates from RH-conditional estimates
bind any use of an incomplete Li cutoff to the exact cutoff/error theorem rather than heuristic truncation
disanalogies: the automorphic generality contains representation-specific constants not all needed for zeta
an estimate proved under RH cannot be repurposed as an unconditional route
localizing the residual does not itself bound or sign it
method_transfers.repair_question: After removing the source-proved archimedean main term, what is the weakest unconditional zeta-specific condition on the finite-place/incomplete-Li residual that is uniform in n and strictly weaker than RH?

preserve hypotheses on zero counts and computation
use the result as a structural calibration for zeta rather than importing a generalized theorem outside its scope

method_transfers.method: reuse the exact hostile-control pattern: preserve the structural symmetry and aggregate statistics of the proposed surrogate while planting one root-critical off-line defect, then ask whether the proposed all-n inference survives

explicit_disanalogies: A radial-outlier synthetic multiset is a logical calibration, not evidence that zeta has an off-critical zero.
A zero-density theorem can be valuable for many analytic estimates while still being insufficient for a Li power-sum bound that is sensitive to one radial outlier.
An exact arithmetic formula is not manifest positivity; cancellations and regularization remain load-bearing.
The unconditional archimedean asymptotic does not imply the finite-place term is small.
A bound equivalent to excluding every off-line zero is a reformulation of RH, not a strictly weaker bridge.
Finite numerical verification of zeros or Li coefficients remains calibration only.

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A large system may have excellent average spectral statistics and only one unstable mode. Repeated powers are eventually governed by that mode, so counting how few unstable modes exist cannot replace a bound on the spectral radius.
common_abstraction: many individually transformed components are aggregated
power iteration amplifies components according to radial magnitude
a rare outlier may dominate an asymptotic or all-index quantity
source_to_target_mapping: eigenvalue radial magnitude -> |rho/(rho-1)| or the reciprocal Li radial factor
time/power index -> Li coefficient index n
unstable mode count -> off-critical zero count/density
shared_constraints: power amplification is exponential in the iteration/index
aggregate counts alone do not bound the largest radial factor
a useful stability theorem must control the outlier coordinate or compensate it by a separately proved cancellation
disanalogies: Li sums contain phase, conjugation and functional-equation symmetry rather than a positive matrix norm
zeros are not freely chosen eigenvalues of a known finite-dimensional operator
the analogy provides a falsification pattern only, not a theorem about zeta
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before using zero density as a Li-tail surrogate, isolate the maximum/weighted radial amplification and test a one-outlier world that satisfies the same count bound.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Derive the target radial factor exactly from the Li zero formula, preserve quartet symmetry, and show only that density/counting premises alone permit the hostile world; do not infer existence of such a zeta zero.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-only structural analogy used to choose a hostile logical calibration; it creates no RH authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Retained the rare-unstable-mode analogy because the shared mathematical mechanism is explicit power amplification by radial magnitude. Rejected generic 'needle in a haystack' and anomaly-detection metaphors as too weak to specify the Li transform or a falsifier.
